notes: CROSS-BATCH GROUP AUDIT (2026-10-17, see scripts/medcheck-uk/audit/groups-cross-batch.md). This file only holds group memberships that span batches; every member quote was checked FOUND with lib/text.mjs. (1) decongestant: new group for the nasal/oral sympathomimetic decongestants (xylometazoline and the four pseudoephedrine-containing clinic products); rules whose source names decongestants or vasoconstrictor amines target it. (2) sympathomimetic is now the broad group (decongestants via batch T/S members plus the beta-2 agonist inhalers listed here); rules whose source says 'sympathomimetics' or 'adrenergic drugs' broadly target it. (3) inhaled-antimuscarinic: new group; tiotropium, ipratropium and the triple inhaler were moved out of the systemic 'anticholinergic' group (batches U, V, X), and only the rules whose UK source covers inhaled antimuscarinics for that interaction (hyoscine butylbromide naming tiotropium/ipratropium; ipratropium and tiotropium 'other anticholinergic drugs') have companion rules for this group. (4) hepatotoxic: added medicines whose own SmPC section 4.4 warns of serious or fatal liver injury. Not added (statement only in the 4.8 table, a class statement, or only in overdose/special populations): see the audit log. (5) aminoglycoside: filled with the gentamicin and neomycin products (ingredient-level UK quotes; four are no-uk-product clinic combinations, added the same way batch T added its no-uk-product combinations) so that allergy cross-reactivity rules reach them; local products are still not matched by other medicines' systemic group interaction rules (engine local-route rule). (6) benzodiazepine: chlordiazepoxide/clidinium (no-uk-product) added from the UK chlordiazepoxide SmPC (Librium 5 mg) so that opioid/CNS-depressant benzodiazepine warnings reach it; clidinium has no UK source, so it is NOT added to anticholinergic. Groups that rules point at and that still have no master-list member: carbapenem, monobactam, maoi, ototoxic (no master-list medicine has a UK source calling it ototoxic as a class; furosemide and the aminoglycoside drops have their own explicit rules).
